title: Random forest model validated for immunotherapy response in head and neck cancer
summary: A random forest model using clinical, laboratory and genomic features, described earlier in a pan-cancer cohort, was validated in recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. AUC for tumor response was 0.65 and accuracy 0.72; stratification gave overall survival HR 0.53 (p=0.045) and progression-free survival HR 0.49 (p=0.016). Performance is modest and the cohort size is not stated in the abstract.
ai_technology: Random forest model using 11 or 16 clinical, laboratory and genomic features

evidence.tested: Cancer-type-specific validation in a new cohort of treated patients.
evidence.unknown: Cohort size and generalizability are not stated or established; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Estimated each patient's likelihood of immune-checkpoint response.
